subject: physics
question_text: What is the value of the acceleration of a freely falling body?

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: The value
lines: A freely falling body has only gravity acting
on it, so its acceleration is g:

lines.text: g = 9.8 m s⁻² (about 9.8, often taken as 10)

steps.why: Free fall means no force other than gravity, so the acceleration is the same for every body regardless of its mass.
common_mistakes: Giving the value without the unit. The unit is part of the answer.
Saying a heavier body falls with a larger acceleration.

recall.must_convey: That the acceleration of a freely falling body is g, about 9.8 metre per second squared.

steps.memory_tip: g = 9.8 m s⁻², the same for every body, whatever its mass.
steps.margin_note: Number AND unit. Both are needed.

steps.label: The direction
lines: towards the centre of the earth, and stays
downward even while the body is rising.
steps.why: The direction is set by the force, not by the motion, which is why g still points down while a body thrown upward is still going up.
common_mistakes: Saying the acceleration points upward while the body rises.

recall.must_convey: That the acceleration is directed vertically downwards, towards the centre of the earth.
accept: towards the centre of the earth

steps.memory_tip: g points down always — even while the body is still going up.
steps.margin_note: Acceleration is a vector. The direction earns this mark.

insider_note: Asked in AP March 2026. Give the number with its unit and its direction — a bare number is an incomplete answer.
